title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL queries with user-controlled input. All database operations use Django ORM methods (objects.get(), objects.filter(), objects.fetch_for_project()) with parameterized queries. The rule_id is passed as an integer parameter to the .get(id=rule_id) method, which uses bound parameters.

The authorization vulnerability (IDOR) has been fixed. Previously, get_rule() fetched rules by ID without ownership verification. Now, convert_args() properly scopes the queryset to the project: for AlertRule it uses fetch_for_project(project), and for Rule it uses filter(project=project). This ensures the user-controlled rule_id can only match rules within the accessed project, preventing cross-project access. The endpoint inherits from ProjectEndpoint which validates project access via ProjectAlertRulePermission.

evidence.content:
def test_cannot_mute_unowned_alert(self):
        user2 = self.create_user("foo@example.com")
        org2 = self.create_organization(name="Other Org", owner=user2)
        project2 = self.create_project(organization=org2, name="Other Project")
        self.login_as(user2)
        response = self.get_error_response(
            org2.slug,
            project2.slug,
            self.issue_alert_rule.id,
            target="everyone",
            status_code=404,
        )
        assert response.data["detail"] == "Rule does not exist"
